open-question.question: The settings view duplicates, renames, deletes, and changes the model and effort of shipped variants and shipped single-task lines, never changing the shipped file: an edit writes a stored copy or a hiding record to the per-user store. A person's hand-written own recipe file (`~/.gurita/recipes.md` by default) also brings recipes, variants, and single-task lines into the merged list, and the extension has never written that file. Does the settings view list the recipes, variants, and single-task lines that come from the hand-written own recipe file, and which of its edits does it offer on them?
open-question.recommendation: One rule covers every item whatever file it came from: the settings view applies the same edits through the same stored copies, hiding records, and reset it already has for shipped items, with no edit set that differs by source and no write to the hand-written file. An own variant of a fixed-name button recipe can then be picked as the default it runs, and the cost named, a stored copy hiding a later hand edit until reset, is the one a shipped variant's stored copy already carries against a later release.
open-question.alternative: The settings view lists own-file items and gives them exactly the edits shipped items get: duplicate, rename, delete, model and effort change, and default pick. Every change to an own item writes a stored copy or a hiding record to the per-user store, never touching the own recipe file, and a reset removes them so the hand-written item shows again. One uniform rule for every item whatever its source: the view behaves identically on shipped and own items, and the extension never writes the hand-written file, as it never has. The person now has two places shaping the same own item, the file they edit by hand and the overlay they made in the view, and a stored copy hides any later hand edit of that item until it is reset, while a hand rename leaves the copy or hiding record orphaned. If the per-user store turns out to be the own recipe file itself, which is decided elsewhere, an overlay of an item in the same file stops making sense.

The settings view does not list the recipes, variants, or single-task lines that come from the own recipe file. It shows and edits only shipped items and the ones the per-user store holds. Own-file items still reach the mission page and the looped run through the merged list, and they are changed only by editing the file by hand. None of them can be picked as a recipe's default in the view. The view keeps one source of truth per item. It edits what the extension owns or overlays, the hand-written file stays entirely the person's, and no rule is needed for how a stored copy or hiding record relates to a line the person may rewrite by hand at any time. Own items are invisible in the one place recipes are managed, so the view's picture of a recipe's variants is incomplete. An own variant can never be a recipe's default, and the seven fixed-name buttons run only their default, so an own variant of one of those recipes could never run from its button. How much this costs depends on how a hand-written recipe of a shipped name combines with the shipped variants, which is decided elsewhere.

The settings view lists own-file recipes, variants, and single-task lines beside shipped and stored ones, each marked as coming from the own recipe file. They can be picked as a recipe's default but take no edit: no duplicate, rename, delete, or model and effort change. They change only through hand edits of the file. Every variant a button can run is visible, and every variant can be picked as the default, so an own variant of a fixed-name button recipe can be made the one it runs. The extension still writes nothing that refers to a hand-written line except the default pick it already stores per recipe. The person sees an own item next to fully editable shipped ones but cannot even copy it, so a quick model or effort change to an own variant means opening the file. A default picked by name is lost when the person renames or deletes that variant by hand, and falls back like any deleted default.

The settings view lists own-file items, marked as such, lets them be picked as a recipe's default, and offers duplicate on them. The duplicate is a new stored item in the per-user store, fully editable like any duplicate. Rename, delete, and model and effort changes are not offered on the own-file item itself, which changes only by hand. Every own item can be built on from the view without the extension ever overlaying or writing a hand-written line. A duplicate is an independent stored item, so nothing stored depends on the own item keeping its name or content. Tuning an own variant from the view leaves two near-identical variants, the hand-written one and its stored copy, unless the person deletes the original by hand. The edit set differs by where an item came from, which the view has to explain.

The settings view lists own-file items, marked as such, lets them be picked as default, and offers duplicate and the model and effort change on them. A model or effort change writes a stored copy to the per-user store that stands in for the own item and keeps its place, removed by a reset as for shipped items. Rename and delete are not offered, since those are structural changes the person makes in the file. The frequent edit, changing a line's model or effort, works the same on every item in the view, while the changes that alter an item's identity stay where the person wrote it, so an overlay never renames or hides a hand-written line out from under the file. A stored copy is keyed to the own item's name, so a later hand rename orphans it and a hand edit of the lines is silently hidden behind it until reset. The edit set still differs by source, now in a subtler split than duplicate-only.

The settings view lists own-file items and offers the full edit set on them, but carries out each edit in the own recipe file itself: a model or effort change rewrites the line, a rename rewrites the `###` heading, a delete removes the recipe block, a duplicate adds a block, and no stored copy or hiding record is made for an own item. Shipped items keep the overlay behaviour already decided, and a default pick is stored as for any recipe. The own item has one true form, the file's text, so the view and the person's hand edits never diverge and there is nothing to reset or orphan. It ends the rule that the extension never writes the hand-written file: every edit has to parse and re-render a file the person may be editing at the same moment, may hold prose and formatting the reader ignores, and has never been written by code, so a careless write can damage hand-made content. Its fit depends on which file holds the variants the view writes, which is decided elsewhere.
